entry_conditions: Observed entry support is the beginning of the red-to-buffer slice: the arm is at the home joint posture, finger width is about 0.08 m, tcp_pose is high above the table, red_pose is in the lower region that is also blue_goal, and blue_pose is in the upper region that is red_goal. The policy may also be invoked partway through this transition because it observes the current qpos/qvel, tcp_pose, red_pose, blue_pose and goal fields causally, not an internal clock.
exit_conditions: The desired handoff is reached when red_pose is on the tabletop near the central buffer around [-0.181, 0.0, 0.02] in world metres, blue_pose remains near the upper/red-goal region, and the gripper/TCP state is compatible with the demonstrated overlap: fingers open and TCP retreating high above the buffer near index 320, or later TCP descending near blue with fingers closing by the end of the overlap.
overlap_role: The expanded slice includes the shared [320,460) transition. In this interval red is already buffered while the arm leaves the buffer, travels toward the blue block, and begins blue acquisition. The policy learns this continuation as diffusion-imitation conditioned on the observed red_buffered state, rather than stopping immediately at geometric placement.
successor_readiness: A successor blue-to-goal policy should receive red buffered on the table, blue still available at the upper/red-goal region, and the robot either open/high after buffer release or already in the low near-blue contact phase supported by the overlap. Causal cues are finger qpos channels, tcp_pose relative to blue_pose, blue_pose remaining at red_goal, and red_pose remaining near the central buffer.
failure_signatures: Observed or likely bad handoff states include red still in the lower blue-goal region, red carried high instead of released, red placed near the upper red-goal/blue start region, red outside the demonstrated central buffer band, blue displaced before the red buffer placement is established, or fingers/TCP not matching either the open retreat or near-blue acquisition modes.
continuation_guidance: Continue this policy through release if red_buffered is not yet true, and continue into the overlap if the robot is still retreating from the buffer or approaching blue. Transfer can be considered once red_buffered is stable from red_pose, blue_pose is still in the upper region, and the successor can use the current TCP/finger relation to continue blue acquisition. The geometric subgoal alone may occur before the transition motion is ready for a clean successor takeover.
limitations: These handoff cues summarize measured demonstration support and the API-authored heuristic; they are not hard safety constraints and do not prove recovery from an occupied buffer, failed grasp, or large out-of-distribution block poses. Contact/grasp status is inferred only from finger width, TCP/object proximity and object motion in state observations.
